messages:
anya: Heads-up: ap-southeast cohort gnode-wearwave-7 causing intermittent GPU attach stalls. 27 pending.
michael: saw IOPS tails on nvme0 across 6 hosts, %util sticky ~100% for minutes. any kernel errors?
ravi: found several `nvme_core: Admin command timeout` and `blk_update_request: I/O error` in dmesg on 3 hosts. snippet in thread.
anya: paste:
```
[ 9876.001234] nvme nvme0: Admin command timeout
[ 9876.001500] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 2345678
```
michael: this cohort got a background wear-leveling/trim job scheduled overnight. looks like trim + heavy provisioning = write amp.
anya: mitigation idea: pause background janitor/trim on cohort, move autoscaler to exclude pool, and cordon noisy nodes.
oncall: ops-bot alert: "GPU_PROVISIONING_HOLD ap-southeast1: 27 pending" at 1791122300
ravi: toggled maintenance flag: `trim.enabled=false` for label cohort=gnode-wearwave-7. cordoning 6 nodes now.
michael: after cordons attach success moved from ~35% to ~85%. still mark 3 drives as degraded for RMA.
anya: ops: prepare cost note if we spill >20% to us-west. brief SLA breach risk otherwise.
oncall: incident INC-2026-1983 opened, tagging hw/storage. scheduling drive replacements for flagged hosts.
ravi: follow-ups: 1) add alert for nvme admin timeouts >2 in 5m; 2) change scrub/trim schedule to avoid peak provisioning window; 3) add autoscaler rule to prefer healthy pools when local-disk errors spike.
anya: will add Grafana panel and run cohort health sweep tomorrow. re-enable trim in 1.5h with lower concurrency. :thumbsup:
michael: logging note: expose nvme admin timeout counter as disk SLI. closing for now.
